title: LLM inference serving, Part 5: scheduling under load
tldr: How an LLM server decides whose work runs in each step when it is overloaded: why one long prompt freezes every stream inside a continuous-batching loop, chunked prefill and Sarathi-Serve's stall-free batching, how vLLM v0.31.0's max_num_batched_tokens trades the worst inter-token gap against long-prompt TTFT (on by default, 8,192 on an H100), head-of-line blocking and long_prefill_token_threshold, SLOs and goodput per DistServe and vllm bench serve, FCFS versus priority scheduling and what priority does not do, queue caps that answer 503, what preemption costs its victim, what breaks first at 10 times the load and the vLLM metrics that show it, a noisy-neighbour tenant, OS time-slicing and API-gateway analogies and where they break, a step-through budget diagram, a chunk-budget calculator, a tested simulator and an interview drill.
